description: Iran's Schengen refusal rate was 26.33% in 2024 (42,653 refusals), down from 30.3% in 2023, against a Schengen-wide average of about 14.6%. Sweden refused 51.57% of Iranian applicants; France refused the most in absolute terms, 10,051 of 39,146.
money_note: Schengen fee is not refunded on refusal.

description: Iran's FY2023 adjusted refusal rate for B visitor visas was 53.26% - among the highest in the world, alongside Pakistan.
source_name: US Dept of State FY23 adjusted refusal rates

description: Most application forms ask whether a visa has ever been refused by any country. A single refusal must then be declared for life, and is weighed against the applicant everywhere else.
energy_note: A permanent mark generated by a discretionary decision with no reasons.
notes: Standard question on UK, Canadian, Australian and US forms.

aspect: No appeal on most visitor refusals
description: UK visitor refusals carry no right of appeal and no administrative review; Schengen refusals have an appeal route that differs by member state and is rarely used successfully from Iran.

Refusal reasoning commonly turns on 'ties to home country' - property, dependants, stable employment. A young, single, childless man scores worst on every limb of that test, which is a gendered outcome produced by a facially neutral rule.
notes: Mechanism is documented in visa guidance generally; per-nationality gender breakdowns are not published. Layer-5 target.

aspect: EXAMPLE - Sweden refused more than half
description: Sweden refused 51.57% of Iranian Schengen applicants in 2024 while Switzerland approved 90.25%. The same applicant, the same file, a different consulate - and opposite odds.
energy_note: Outcome determined by which flag is on the building.

aspect: EXAMPLE - the money kept on refusal
description: Schengen states refused 42,653 Iranian applications in 2024. At EUR 90 each, roughly EUR 3.8 million in non-refundable fees was collected from refused Iranian applicants in a single year.

aspect: SCENARIO - the refusal he must declare forever
description: Maryam is refused a Schengen visa in 2019 for 'intention to leave the territory could not be ascertained'. In 2024 she applies to Canada. Question 2(b): have you ever been refused a visa by any country? She answers yes, attaches an explanation, and spends four months in additional review because of a five-year-old refusal that came with no reasons she could rebut.
energy_note: One unexplained no, declared for the rest of your life.
